theme: 教材字彙・基礎 550–650 第 26 群

items.pos: v. 收費；控告 | n. 費用；責任
items.colloc: charge a fee 收取費用 | in charge of 負責
items.distinct: cost 成本 | price 價格
ex: They will charge a fee for the extra service.
他們將為額外服務收取費用。
Who is currently in charge of this project?
目前是誰負責這個專案？
Please charge the purchase to the company account.
請將這筆採購記在公司帳上。
The speaker explained the strategy very clearly.
演講者非常清晰地解釋了策略。
It is clearly stated in the contract terms.
合約條款中已明確記載。
The instructions were not written clearly enough.
這些說明寫得不夠清楚。

items.pos: n. 評論；意見 | v. 發表意見
items.colloc: make a comment 發表評論 | negative comment 負面評價
items.distinct: remark 簡短評論 | opinion 個人看法
ex: We appreciate your comments on the new design.
我們感謝您對新設計提供的意見。
The manager refused to comment on the rumor.
經理拒絕針對該傳聞發表評論。
Please leave your comments in the suggestion box.
請將您的意見留在意見箱中。

items.pos: adj. 商業的 | n. 商業廣告
items.colloc: commercial success 商業成功 | commercial bank 商業銀行
items.distinct: advertisement 一般廣告 | marketing 行銷
ex: The company achieved great commercial success this year.
公司今年獲得了巨大的商業成功。
They aired a new commercial during the game.
他們在比賽期間播放了一支新廣告。
This building is zoned for commercial use only.
這棟建築僅限於商業用途。

items.pos: adj. 完全的；完整的 | v. 完成
items.colloc: complete the task 完成任務 | complete set 整套
items.distinct: finish 結束某事 | entire 全部
ex: Please complete the registration form by Friday.
請在週五前完成註冊表格。
The team is waiting for the complete report.
團隊正在等待完整的報告。
It took two weeks to complete the renovation.
花費兩週時間才完成裝修。

items.colloc: attend a conference 參加會議 | annual conference 年度會議
items.distinct: meeting 例會 | convention 大會
ex: The international conference will be held in Taipei.
國際研討會將在台北舉辦。
She is attending a conference on renewable energy.
她正在參加關於再生能源的會議。
Registration for the upcoming conference is now open.
即將到來的會議開放報名中。

items.colloc: feel confident 感到自信 | confident in 對…有信心
items.distinct: certain 確定的 | optimistic 樂觀的
ex: The CEO is confident about the market outlook.
執行長對市場前景充滿信心。
You need to be confident during the presentation.
你在簡報時需要展現自信。
Our team is confident that we will win.
我們團隊確信我們會贏得比賽。

items.colloc: serious consequence 嚴重後果 | as a consequence 因此
items.distinct: result 結果 | outcome 結局
ex: You must consider the consequences of this decision.
你必須考慮這個決定的後果。
Failure to follow rules has serious consequences.
未遵守規則會導致嚴重後果。
As a consequence, the project was delayed.
因此，該專案延遲了。

items.pos: v. 跳舞 | n. 舞蹈；舞會
items.colloc: dance performance 舞蹈表演 | dance party 舞會
items.distinct: ball 舞會 | choreography 編舞
ex: We will hire a performer to dance tonight.
我們今晚會雇用一名表演者跳舞。
The company will host a dance for the staff.
公司將為員工舉辦一場舞會。
She practiced her dance moves for the show.
她為演出練習了舞蹈動作。

items.pos: v. 處理；交易 | n. 協議；交易
items.colloc: deal with 處理 | sign a deal 簽署協議
items.distinct: arrangement 安排 | contract 合約
ex: Our team can deal with difficult clients easily.
我們的團隊能輕鬆處理困難的客戶。
Both parties have finally signed the business deal.
雙方終於簽署了這項商業協議。
We need a better deal from our supplier.
我們需要從供應商那邊獲得更好的交易。

items.colloc: disappoint someone 使某人失望 | be disappointed 對…失望
items.distinct: let down 辜負 | discourage 打擊信心
ex: The poor sales figures will disappoint the investors.
慘淡的銷售數據會讓投資者失望。
I do not want to disappoint our regular customers.
我不想讓我們的忠實客戶失望。
He was disappointed by the lack of feedback.
他對缺乏回饋感到失望。

items.colloc: natural disaster 天然災害 | financial disaster 財務危機
items.distinct: tragedy 悲劇 | failure 失敗
ex: The marketing campaign was a complete disaster.
這次的行銷活動是一場徹底的失敗。
Emergency plans were ready for any potential disaster.
緊急計畫已為任何潛在災難做好準備。
They worked hard to prevent an economic disaster.
他們努力防止一場經濟災難。

items.colloc: have a discussion 進行討論 | open for discussion 開放討論
items.distinct: debate 辯論 | conversation 對話
ex: The manager opened a discussion about the budget.
經理開啟了關於預算的討論。
This topic is still open for further discussion.
這個話題仍開放進一步討論。
We had a long discussion about the future.
我們針對未來進行了一場長談。

items.colloc: sales division 銷售部門 | create a division 劃分
items.distinct: department 部門 | section 部分
ex: He works in the international marketing division.
他在國際行銷部門工作。
The division of labor helped increase productivity.
勞動分工有助於提升生產力。
Each division must submit its monthly report.
每個部門都必須提交月度報告。

items.pos: n. 影響；效力 | v. 造成
items.colloc: have an effect on 對…有影響 | side effect 副作用
items.distinct: affect 影響（動詞）| influence 影響力
ex: The new policy will have an immediate effect.
這項新政策將會有立即的影響。
Smoking has a bad effect on your health.
抽菸對你的健康有不良影響。
The law will come into effect next month.
這項法律將於下個月生效。

items.colloc: make an effort 做出努力 | joint effort 共同努力
items.distinct: attempt 嘗試 | struggle 掙扎
ex: The success was the result of our joint effort.
這次成功是我們共同努力的結果。
You need to make more effort to improve.
你需要投入更多努力來改進。
They put a lot of effort into the project.
他們在該專案上投入了大量心力。

items.colloc: emerge from 從…中出現 | newly emerged 新興的
items.distinct: appear 顯現 | arrive 到達
ex: New opportunities began to emerge in the market.
市場上開始出現新的機會。
The company emerged as a leader in tech.
該公司崛起成為科技領域的領導者。
True facts will emerge after the investigation.
真相將在調查後浮出水面。

items.colloc: potential employer 潛在雇主 | employer-employee 勞資
items.distinct: employee 員工 | manager 主管
ex: The employer provides health insurance for staff.
雇主為員工提供健康保險。
You should research the employer before interviewing.
面試前你應該先調查該雇主。
The employer wants to increase overall wages.
雇主想要提高整體薪資。

items.colloc: excellent performance 優異表現 | excellent service 優質服務
items.distinct: good 好的 | superior 上等的
ex: The restaurant is famous for its excellent service.
這家餐廳以優質服務聞名。
She has an excellent track record in sales.
她在銷售方面有非常優異的紀錄。
Thank you for your excellent work this month.
謝謝你這個月表現得非常出色。

items.pos: n. 主管；行政人員 | adj. 執行的
items.colloc: chief executive 執行長 | executive suite 高階主管套房
items.distinct: manager 經理 | director 董事
ex: The chief executive will attend the board meeting.
執行長將出席董事會會議。
Our company is looking for a new executive.
我們公司正在尋找一位新主管。
He works in an executive office downtown.
他在市中心的一間行政辦公室工作。
